_help: The Pirate's Handbook. Each chapter is a button on the left of the book. Lines in 'text': '# ' = heading, '- ' = bullet point, '> ' = tip, '' = empty line, anything else = normal text. Pages are split up by themselves. 'icon' is any item id, 'color' is a hex colour.

chapters.title: Welcome Aboard
text: You want to be a pirate? Good. This handbook explains everything you need to know, one chapter at a time. Click a chapter on the left, and use the arrows (or your mouse wheel) to turn pages.
# Your first hour
The First Voyage guide shows in your inventory and walks you through it in five parts:
- Castaway: choose your race, open this journal, the One Piece Keys list (Esc menu), your HUD (H) and your quest tree (J).
- Set Sail: get in your boat, read your Log Pose, find Foosha Village and help Luffy (Chapter 1 of the story).
- Pirate Life: train to Pirate Level 1 and spend your stat point (K), start a crew and hire your first crewmate.
- Captain: build any floating hull, put a Ship's Wheel on it and take the helm.
- Devil Fruit: find one, eat it and use its power. Fruits are rare, so this part can take a while!
Tips pop up in chat the first time you need a new key: your first Haki, fighting style, ship's helm and more.
> /tutorial lists every step. /tutorial skip skips one, /tutorial off hides the guide and tips, /tutorial on brings them back.
# How progress works

This mod is slow on purpose. A full voyage takes 20 to 50 hours. Most strong things are locked behind bosses, bounty, Haki or islands you've visited. If something is locked, the game always tells you what you still need.
> Lost this book? Type /guide to get a new one.

chapters.title: Keys & Commands
text: # Keys
- R: Devil Fruit main move. Sneak + R: second move.
- Y: awakening progress, or your awakened form once you have it.
- V: Observation Haki on/off. B: Armament Haki on/off. G: release Conqueror's Haki.
- Z: use your fighting style technique. Shift + Z: pick the next technique.
- On a ship: W / S to sail and slow down, A / D to turn, sneak to jump off.
> You can change every key in Options, Controls, Key Binds.
# Commands for everyone
- /story, /story chapters, /story chart, /story log
- /race, /race list
- /haki
- /style, /style use <style>
- /crew, /crew create <name>, /crew hire <role> [1-3], /crew blueprint, /crew dismiss <role>, /crew disband
- /bounty, /bounty check <player>, /bounty poster
- /empire
- /guide (a new copy of this book)

chapters.title: Races
text: The first time you join, you choose a race. Each one has perks and drawbacks, and you can never change it, so read carefully. Your race stays after you die.
# The ten races
- Human: Haki trains 50% faster. No body powers.
- Fish-Man: breathe and mine underwater, fast swimming, +2 attack. Slower on land.
- Mink: faster, jump higher, night vision, Electro punches. Hungry in hot places.
- Giant: 1.5x size, +5 hearts, +2 attack, more reach. Too tall for doors, always hungry.
- Skypiean: Observation trains 2x, safe falls. Fewer hearts.
- Lunarian: immune to fire and lava and well armored while dry. Weak in water and rain.
- Long-Arm Tribe: +2 blocks reach. Slower swings.
- Long-Leg Tribe: faster, jump higher. One heart less.
- Tontatta Dwarf: half size, fast, strong, digs fast. 3 hearts less.
- Oni: armor, attack and knockback. Slower and hungrier.
> Not sure? Human is the easiest start. Fish-Man is great for a sea-heavy game.
# Commands
- /race shows your race and perks. /race list shows all of them.
- /race pick opens the screen again if you closed the game before picking.

chapters.title: Devil Fruits
text: There are 108 Devil Fruits. Eat one to get its power forever. Eat a second one and you die!
# Finding a fruit
- Leaves have a tiny chance (about 1 in 2,000) to drop one. Early in the story only weaker fruits drop.
- Every boss drops their own fruit when you beat them.
# Using your power
- R uses the main move, Sneak + R the second one. Hover over a fruit to see its moves.
- Logia users (fire, ice, light...) dodge half of all attacks, unless the attacker uses Armament Haki.
- Many fruits give passive powers too, like Gomu Gomu's no fall damage.
> Every fruit you find is recorded in the Devil Fruit Encyclopedia (Book + Gold Ingot + Ink Sac).
# Weaknesses
- In water you get weak, you sink, and you can't use your power.
- Seastone does the same: holding it, standing on it, or getting hit by a Seastone weapon.
> Fruit users should hire a helmsman. They pull you out of the water.
# Awakening (very hard)
- Reach 1,000 mastery: each move that hits an enemy gives 1. Dying costs a tenth.
- Beat 5 different story bosses.
- Finish the Wano chapter of the story.
- Then, the next time something would kill you, your fruit awakens instead.
Press Y to see your progress. Once awakened, Y turns on your awakened form.

chapters.title: Haki
text: Haki is willpower made real. Anyone can learn it. Each kind has levels 1 to 5. Type /haki to see your levels and what to do next.
# Observation (V)
- Train it by getting hit by mobs. Getting hit while Blind counts 5 times.
- Gives a chance to dodge attacks (up to 35%). While sneaking, nearby creatures glow through walls.
# Armament (B)
- Train it by punching mobs with your bare hands.
- When on: extra damage, extra armor, and your hits land on Logia users.
- It uses hunger and turns off when you're too hungry.
# Conqueror's (G)
- Rare. 1 in 100 players is born with it.
- Otherwise, the first time you beat each boss there's a 2% to 10% chance it awakens.
- Releasing it knocks out weak monsters nearby and freezes stronger ones.
# Lessons
Silvers Rayleigh teaches Haki for Berries. Sneak and right-click him. His lessons open at Sabaody in the story.
> Humans train Haki 50% faster, and Skypieans train Observation twice as fast.

chapters.title: Fighting Styles
text: Ten masters can teach you their way of fighting. Type /style to see every style, what each master wants, and your moves.
# Learning a style
- Find the master and sneak + right-click them. They ask for Berries and items, and some want you to have beaten bosses first.
- Can't find them? Right-click their Vivre Card. It points to their home. Get within 48 blocks and use it again: the master appears.
- You can know several styles. Switch with /style use <style>.
# The styles
- Santoryu (Zoro): three swords.
- Black Leg (Sanji): kicks with an empty hand.
- Fish-Man Karate (Jinbe): punches, double strength in water.
- Rokushiki (Koby): Soru, Geppo, Tekkai...
- Ryusoken (Sabo): crushing dragon claws.
- Oden Nitoryu (Oden): a sword in each hand.
- Kitsunebi-ryu (Kin'emon): flame swords.
- Soul King Fencing (Brook): freezing cuts.
- Fist of Love (Garp): huge punches.
- Sogeking Sniping (Usopp): bow and crossbow shots.
# Using techniques
Z uses your technique, Shift + Z picks the next. Moves cost hunger and have cooldowns. The last technique of each style unlocks when you beat a certain boss.
> Armament Haki makes every technique 25% stronger.

chapters.title: Crafting Stations
text: The mod's gear isn't made at a crafting table. You make it at five crafting stations. Each one leads to the next.
# How they work
- Right-click a station to see everything it makes. No grid: just carry the ingredients and press Craft.
- White = you can make it now. Yellow = missing ingredients. Red = locked, and the screen says why.
# The five stations
- 1. Shipwright's Bench: ship parts, cannons, figureheads, guns and ammo.
- 1. Ship's Galley: food like Pirate Bento, Sea King Stew and Rumble Balls.
- 2. Navigator's Desk (needs a Ship's Wheel): Log Pose, Eternal Pose, Sea Charts, Den Den Mushi, Dials.
- 3. Seastone Workbench (needs Seastone Ingots): Seastone Cuffs, Jitte, Sea King armor.
- 4. Swordsmith's Forge (needs a Seastone Jitte, so beat Smoker first): famous swords and weapon upgrades.
> You build the stations themselves at a normal crafting table. Look them up in your recipe book.
> Stations also work on the deck of a sailing ship.

chapters.title: Using the Journal
text: # Using the journal
This journal knows every item, Devil Fruit, creature, boss, character and place in the mod.
- Click a bookmark on the side of the book to open a topic.
- The left page explains the topic. The right page lists everything in it.
- Click an entry to open its page: what it is, how to get it and what it's used in.
- In a recipe, click any item to jump to its page. Right-click to see what it's used in.
- Type in the search box to search the whole journal.
- Esc or "< Back" goes back a page. The mouse wheel turns pages.
> Gold lines like "Requires: Beat Smoker" are locks: do that first before a station will make the item.
> Want a list of every item beside your inventory? Install JEI. It works with this mod.

chapters.title: The Story
text: The main story follows the road to Laugh Tale in 26 chapters, from Foosha Village to the end of the Grand Line.
# Your Captain's Log
- You get it the first time you join. Right-click it, or type /story, to see your chapter, goals and reward.
- Goals tick off by themselves. When they're all done, the next chapter starts.
- Each chapter gives you Sea Charts to the places it needs. Lost one? /story chart (costs 1 Paper).
# The sagas
- Romance Dawn: your first crewmate and your first boat.
- East Blue: Buggy, the Baratie, Arlong Park and Reverse Mountain.
- Paradise: from Drum Island to Sabaody.
- Summit War: Amazon Lily, Marineford and two years of training.
- New World: from Fish-Man Island to Wano.
- Final Saga: Blackbeard, and the treasure at Laugh Tale.
# Story gates

Some shortcuts wait for the story, so the journey can't be skipped: a villain's Wanted Poster only works after you beat them at their lair, awakening opens after Wano, and Laugh Tale needs all four Road Poneglyph rubbings.
> If you die during a story event, it stops. Go back to the place and try again.

chapters.title: Characters & Quests
text: 52 characters from One Piece live in the world. Some are bosses, some give quests, some run shops.
# Bosses
- Each boss waits in their own lair. They have a health bar and special attacks from their story.
- Beating one gives Berries, bounty and their Devil Fruit.
- After that, their Wanted Poster calls them back for a Hard rematch, then Expert. Better prizes each time.
- The fruit and prizes only drop the first time you win at each difficulty. Fighting the same difficulty again pays only a few Berries.
# Quest givers
- Right-click them to get a quest step: beat a boss, bring items, or talk to someone.
- Do it, come back, right-click again for the reward. Every giver has 3 or 4 steps.
> A good first quest: Koby.
# Traders
- Right-click to trade for Berries. Like villagers, they level up and unlock new trades.
# Berries
Berries are the money. Bosses drop them, quests pay them, and traders and masters want them.
# Vivre Cards
A Vivre Card points to its owner's home. Right-click it to see the direction and distance.

chapters.title: Your Crew
text: A captain needs a crew. You can hire one crewmate for each of nine roles.
# Hiring
- /crew create <name> makes you captain and gives you a Tavern Blueprint.

- Build a Pirate Tavern: 5x5 plank floor, log posts in the corners (3 high), 5x5 wooden roof, 2 barrels, a lantern, a bed and a Recruitment Board in the middle. Click the ground with the blueprint to see the outline.
- Right-click the Recruitment Board to meet 3 recruits per job, each with their own kind, personality, stats and price. Click [Hire].
- Each hire costs more Berries (10 up to 300) and a trial item.
- Shipwright, archaeologist, musician and helmsman need a bigger crew first.
# The roles
- Swordsman, Navigator, Sniper, Cook, Doctor, Shipwright, Archaeologist, Musician, Helmsman.
- Each one gives you a perk while nearby, like Strength from the swordsman or Haste from the shipwright.
# Giving orders
- Right-click a crewmate: Follow, Wait, Work.
- Work mode: they do their job within 10 blocks. The cook farms and cooks, the doctor heals, the shipwright repairs gear...
- Sneak + right-click opens their bag.
> Put a chest near a working crewmate. They take supplies from it and put what they make into it.
> A Den Den Mushi calls your whole crew to you.

chapters.title: Bounties & the Navy
text: Every pirate has a bounty. Yours starts at 0, and the Marines leave you alone.
# Raising it
- Beat bosses: Buggy adds 15 million, Kaido 1.5 billion. Beating the same boss again adds only 10%.
- Beat Marines: 1 to 20 million each.
- Friends within 32 blocks share the bounty for a boss.
# The Navy hunts you
- The higher your bounty, the more often Marine squads come for you, and the stronger they are.
- At 100 million Smoker may lead the hunt. At 1 billion, an Admiral.
- Get far away for a minute and they give up.
# Navy raids

Now and then the Navy raids where you stand, in waves, with a blue bar at the top of the screen. Beat every wave for Berries and a big bounty jump. Near the sea a warship shows up and fires cannons. Take its wheel to steal it!
> Bounty unlocks gear at the stations, so a higher bounty is worth the danger.
> /bounty shows your bounty and threat level. /bounty poster prints your Wanted Poster.

chapters.title: Ships & Jolly Rogers
text: Build your ship any way you like, out of any blocks, right in the sea.
# Setting sail
- Place a Ship's Wheel on deck while looking toward the front. That's the bow.
- Right-click the wheel. The whole build becomes a ship and you're the captain.
- W / S sails and slows, A / D turns. Friends right-click the ship to climb aboard.
- To dock: stop, then right-click the ship twice.
# Good to know
- Wool blocks and painted Sails make you faster. Big ships need more sails.
- Chests and crafting stations on deck work while you sail.
- Sneaking on deck makes you jump off, into the sea!
# Your Jolly Roger
Hold a Jolly Roger and right-click the air to paint your own flag. Mirror mode is great for skulls. Choose Flag, Sail or Plaque, then Save and right-click a block to hang it.
> Adam wood from the Treasure Tree is the toughest wood for a ship.

chapters.title: Seas & Navigation
text: # The seas
- The Grand Line runs through the middle of the world (Z between -1000 and 1000). Press F3 to see your Z.
- On both sides lies a Calm Belt: no wind, so sails do nothing, and Sea Kings nest there.
- Further out are the Blue seas.
# Sea Kings
Giant sea serpents that knock you off your ship. Very common in the Calm Belt. They drop meat you can cook into Sea King Meat on the Bone.
# Finding your way
- Log Pose: stay on an island for 45 seconds. It records it and points to the next island, always leading onward toward the New World.
- Eternal Pose: points to one island forever. Use it to find your way home.
- Sea Chart: a map with a red X to a place. Charts come from the story and quests.
- Vivre Card: points to a character's home.
- South Birds always face south, like a living compass.
> Some gear needs islands recorded on your Log Pose. Visit lots of islands!

chapters.title: The World
text: # Grand Line world type

When you create a world, open More World Options and click World Type until it says Grand Line. You get a world that is mostly sea, with islands from One Piece: 20 island biomes from East Blue Isle to Onigashima.
# Danger
- Easy islands have farm animals and weak monsters.
- Deadly islands spawn wither skeletons and blazes in the open. Come prepared!
# 80 structures
- Every boss has their own lair, like Buggy's Big Top or Kaido's Onigashima.
- 58 more places from the story: Foosha Village, the Baratie, Water 7, Impel Down...
- Easy places are common. Legendary ones are very rare and very hard, with the best loot.
- They appear in normal worlds too, in matching biomes.
> Structures and island biomes can be found with /locate if cheats are on.

chapters.title: Creatures
text: 40 One Piece animals live in the world, in the Nether, and on the islands.
# Kinds
- Passive ones run away: South Birds, Cotton Candy Lambs, Island Whales...
- Neutral ones fight back: Kung-Fu Dugongs, Yagara Bulls, Krakens...
- Hostile ones hunt you: Lapahns, Bananawani, Sea Cats, Pacifistas...
# Living with them
- Hold a creature's favourite food and it follows you. Feeding a hurt one heals it.
- Some can be tamed: keep feeding them until hearts appear.
- Sneak + right-click a tamed creature to make it stay or follow.
- Some can be ridden.
> Shear a Cotton Candy Lamb for sugar.

chapters.title: Ores & Resources
text: # Ores
- Seastone: under the ocean floor. Smelt it into ingots. Devil Fruit users beware!
- Tamahagane: mountains and Wano. For katanas.
- Wapometal: snowy places. For armor.
- Shandora Gold: badlands, jungles, Skypiea. Turns into Berries.
- Sulfur: deserts, badlands and the Nether. For gunpowder, bullets and cannonballs.
- Kokuto: deep in deepslate, needs a diamond pickaxe. For black blades.
# Other treasures
- Shell Sand on beaches makes Dial Shells.
- Oyster Gravel on the sea floor gives Sea Pearls.
- Yarukiman Resin (bottle on a Yarukiman log) becomes Bubble Coating for breathing underwater.
- Sea King Scales, Kraken Ink and Dragon Scales come from creatures.
# Poneglyphs
Unbreakable red stones. With an archaeologist in your crew, hold Paper and carry Kraken Ink, then right-click a Road Poneglyph to copy it. All four copies open Laugh Tale.

chapters.title: Weapons
text: # Guns
- Right-click to shoot. Ammo in your off hand is used first, so you choose the kind.
- From the Flintlock Pistol to Bege's Tommy Gun. Most are made at the Shipwright's Bench.
- Ammo: bullets, Seastone bullets, cannonballs, and Usopp's stars and Pop Greens.
# Famous weapons
- Many bosses drop their weapon: Kaido's Hassaikai, Whitebeard's Murakumogiri, Mihawk's Yoru...
- Others are forged at the Swordsmith's Forge once you've earned them.
# Upgrades
- New enchantments like Seastone Edge, Haki Coating and Flying Slash.
- Whetstones raise a sword's grade: Skillful, Great, Supreme.
- Guns take scopes, long barrels and hair triggers. Dials add fire or knockback.
> Hold the weapon in your off hand and the upgrade in your main hand, then right-click.

chapters.title: Emperors & Kingdoms
text: The end game. Only the greatest pirates earn a title. Type /empire to see how close you are.
# Pirate kingdoms
- Plant a Kingdom Flag to claim the land around it (48 blocks).
- Pirate guards move in and defend it, more if there are beds.
- Your kingdom pays taxes in Berries every day. Right-click the flag to collect.
# The titles
- Emperor of the Sea: 1 billion bounty, beat an Emperor on Hard, 6+ crewmates, own a kingdom, and finish Wano.
- Pirate King: be an Emperor and finish the story.
- King of the World: Pirate King, 3 billion bounty, beat all four Admirals, and master Conqueror's Haki.
# The price of fame
Titles give more loot, taxes and kingdoms. But the Navy hunts title holders much harder, and may even send a Buster Call.
> On a server only 4 players can be Emperors. Beat a title holder to take their title!

chapters.title: Mining & Drills
text: # Tool tiers
- Adam Wood (Shipwright's Bench): iron-level, but lasts much longer. Needs Adam planks from the rare Treasure Tree Adam.
- Seastone (Seastone Workbench): diamond-level, and the only tier below Sea Prism that cuts Sea Prism Veins. Hits drain Devil Fruit users.
- Sea Prism (Seastone Workbench, after you beat Magellan): the best there is. Only Sea Prism cuts Abyss Stone.
> The Adam wood grips keep a Devil Fruit user safe while holding them.
# Island ores
Every big island hides a material found nowhere else:
- Alabasta: Desert Amber. Fishman Island: Sun Coral. Whole Cake and Cacao: Rock Candy (eat it for Haste).
- Elbaph and Little Garden: Giant Iron. Egghead: Egghead Alloy. Thriller Bark and Kuraigana: Gloom Crystal.
- Zou: Electro Crystal (great drill fuel). Amazon Lily: Snake Jade.
- Wano, Kuri and Impel Down: much richer seastone veins.
- Everywhere, below y -32: Sea Prism Veins (Seastone pickaxe or better).
> Crush a Gloom Crystal to see which ores hide in the rock around you.
# The Mining Drill
Build it at the Shipwright's Bench. Place it facing the rock (it points away from you, so look down for a shaft).
- Right-click with coal, charcoal, sulfur, blaze rods, coal blocks or electro crystals to fuel it (sneak for the whole stack).
- Right-click with a drill bit to fit it. Adam bits dig 32 blocks, Seastone 64, Sea Prism 128.
- Put an Ore Cart (or a chest, barrel or chest minecart) right next to it: that's where everything it digs goes.
- Empty hand: see how it's doing. Sneak + empty hand: switch it on or off.
# Crew miners

Set any crewmate to Work within 6 blocks of a drill and they become its miner: they keep it fuelled from the chests nearby, fit new bits, and haul half-full carts into the chests. While they stand by, the drill digs 40% faster.
# Seastone Deep Mines

Old Impel Down quarries lie deep under the Grand Line: shafts, cell blocks and ore galleries going down level by level, with jailers still on guard. The richest Sea Prism and the Abyss Stone vault are at the bottom.
